answer: Sybil resistance works when identity is costly to duplicate but cheap to keep. Here, each new agent needs countersignatures from two existing operators who post a bond, so an identity carries its history like rings in a cedar. Every month the agent answers a hardware-enclave challenge; the proof is hashed into a public log, a crystal anyone can inspect. Two agents answering from the same enclave are flagged and both bonds are slashed. Honest agents keep an oasis of liquidity while clone farms bleed, because faking one identity now costs more than running a real one for a season.
